reviewer: Captain (source provenance and vehicle mapping from bytes already held; not a counsel approval)
question: Four of the five North Dakota routes have no official source bound, and the fifth names SFN-61663 without provenance. What does the corpus already hold, and what does each route's filing vehicle actually turn out to be?
method: Existing corpus first. No acquisition was performed and none proved necessary for the route this record resolves.

theDefect: official_sources: SFN-61663 does not name the corpus release and archive its bytes were verified from
official_sources: SFN-61663 has no content hash
official_sources: SFN-61663 has no expected content hash from a packet source record
official_sources: SFN-61663 has no installed content hash from a verified corpus

sfn61663.whyItLookedMissing: The form is in the library under a filename that reads as the generic Pardon Advisory Board application -- ND__SUPPORT__ND-NORTH-DAKOTA-PARDON-ADVISORY-BOARD-APPLICA__north-dakota-pardon-advisory-board-application-to-pardon-eligible__REV-2020-02__EN.pdf -- so a search for the form number found nothing. The form number is printed on the document, not in its name.

theBytes.manifestAgreement: STATES/ND/STATE_MANIFEST.csv declares this exact sha256 for document_id ND-NORTH-DAKOTA-PARDON-ADVISORY-BOARD-APPLICA at revision REV-2020-02, source_status acquired_2026-08-02. The bytes on disk hash to the declared value, so the manifest and the file agree rather than one being taken on trust.

theFormIdentifiesItself.printedTitle: NORTH DAKOTA PARDON ADVISORY BOARD APPLICATION TO PARDON ELIGIBLE MARIJUANA OFFENSES
theFormIdentifiesItself.printedIssuer: NORTH DAKOTA DEPARTMENT OF CORRECTIONS AND REHABILITATION
theFormIdentifiesItself.why: This is what closes the provenance gap. The binding does not rest on a filename or on a form number asserted in a memo: the document states its own number and issuer, and the revision the manifest records (REV-2020-02) is the revision the form prints (02-2020).

boundTo.memoLegalName: Application to Pardon Eligible Marijuana Offences (N.D.C.C. ch. 12-55.1; SFN 61663)
boundTo.andNothingElse: Not bound to any other North Dakota route. The memo carries a separate regular-pardon track, nd-regular-pardon, at SFN 14859, and that form is not in the library. One pardon form does not stand in for the other.

whatTheFormSaysAboutItsOwnRelief.printedText: A REQUEST FOR A PARDON WILL NOT EXPUNGE AN INDIVIDUAL'S CRIMINAL HISTORY RECORD.
whatTheFormSaysAboutItsOwnRelief.whyThisMatters: The route is named ...summary-pardon-or-sealing-relief and is marked paid_packet_intended. The controlling form opens by telling the applicant, in capitals, that the relief it provides is not expungement of the criminal history record. Whether this route may be sold as record-clearing relief, and what a participant must be told about what they are buying, is a legal and product question this record raises and does not answer.
whatTheFormSaysAboutItsOwnRelief.disposition: Raised for counsel and for the owner. No route is opened, no packet is composed, and no participant-facing description is written here.

alsoNote.filingIsNotACourtFiling: The memo's filing rule for this track is 'Submit the completed application with its attachments to the pardon clerk by mail, fax or email.' This is an agency submission, not a filing in a court case, so caption, case mode and case-number treatment do not apply to it in the way they do to the other four routes.
alsoNote.deadlineIsOnTheForm: The form states the Pardon Advisory Board meets in April and November and the application must be received 90 days before it convenes. A packet that ignores that timing would be filing-grade and still useless.

vehicleMap.note: Per route, from the memo, which supersedes the Edition 1 legal review's provisional table. Both are recorded because they disagree, and the disagreement is informative.

routes.vehicleDetermination: An official form controls and the corpus holds it. Under the Form vs Custom Pleading rule this route uses that form and may not be given a composed pleading instead.

routes.newUnboundSourceFound: Sealing-DUI-Records-Research-Guide.pdf, North Dakota Legal Self Help Center, 6 pages, sha256 a3dd1b924bedad7c8ba0b77742bcd99ef6855a1b05021374b7083f1b445e1264, present in the Nationwide Recovery Pool and NOT in Edition 1's STATES/ND. It is a research guide, not a form.
routes.vehicleDetermination: Not determined here. A research guide is authority for procedure, not a filing vehicle, and finding one does not establish that no official form exists. Do not draft a custom pleading on the strength of this guide alone.

routes.memoFilingRule: File the motion in the existing criminal case with the clerk of court.

routes.vehicleDetermination: Not determined here. Note that one runtime route currently stands in for three memo tracks with three different statutory subsections, which is the same shape as the Oregon route that had to be split. Flagged, not decided.
routes.relatedSource: Sealing Criminal Records or Closing Nonconviction Court Records (N.D.C.C. Ch. 12-60.1), 17 pages, sha256 b39a0c1532bff3381382544a3888478835edb2109af597a2468a34e2a5f19a3c, already in Edition 1 as a supporting-process guide.

routes.whyTheDisagreementMatters: The review's table would make this route guidance-only, which would sit badly with its paid_packet_intended disposition. The memo supersedes it and describes a two-unit structure -- a verification unit where nothing is filed, and a fallback motion unit filed in the existing criminal case -- so a paid packet is not on its face wrong. Checked before asserting a defect; there is no defect to report.

corpusFindings.twoCollectionsOverlap: The Nationwide Recovery Pool's LegalEase North Dakota folder and Edition 1's STATES/ND hold two files in common, byte-identical: Close-Nonconviction-Records.pdf equals the Edition 1 EXPERTISE instructions at sha256 21b3a790b35f35c345560d9840bf39ca6f1e46cf1b9166c0e5ae2cf8ff7e4d7f, and Sealing Criminal Records Research Guide.pdf equals the Edition 1 supporting-process guide at sha256 b39a0c1532bff3381382544a3888478835edb2109af597a2468a34e2a5f19a3c. Nothing needs re-acquiring.

theAr41SetIsNotForTheseRoutes.what: The Recovery Pool holds a complete seven-document component set for a Motion to Prohibit Public Access under Administrative Rule 41 section 5(f)(1): notice, motion, brief, declaration, findings/conclusions/order, affidavit of service by mail, and a confidential information form. All are North Dakota district court captioned documents.
theAr41SetIsNotForTheseRoutes.whereItBelongs: The memo carries a track for it -- nd-prohibit-remote-public-access, 'Motion to Prohibit Remote Public Access to a Criminal Case Record After Dismissal or Acquittal' -- and the review files it as Track 10, process guidance only.
theAr41SetIsNotForTheseRoutes.doNotBind: It is NOT the vehicle for any of the five routes in scope and must not be bound to them. A complete and attractive component set for a different remedy is exactly the kind of thing that gets borrowed because it is there.

theOneApprovedFormIsNotAmongTheFive.what: The only North Dakota track the Edition 1 review approved for implementation with an official form is Track 2, 'Petition to close pre-August 2025 nonconviction records', N.D.C.C. § 12-60.1-05(2), official_pdf_fill, and the corpus holds its instructions at sha256 21b3a790b35f35c345560d9840bf39ca6f1e46cf1b9166c0e5ae2cf8ff7e4d7f.
theOneApprovedFormIsNotAmongTheFive.andYet: No runtime route in the Grade-A projection corresponds to it. The five North Dakota routes carrying records are the deferred-imposition, DUI, first-offense-possession, general-conviction-sealing and marijuana-pardon routes.
theOneApprovedFormIsNotAmongTheFive.disposition: Recorded as a coverage observation for the owner, not acted on. Opening a route is a product decision and this record opens nothing. It is noted because the state's most build-ready track currently has no route, while four routes that do exist have no official source.

whatRemains: Four of the five routes still have no official source bound, and this record does not draft for any of them: a missing source is not permission to compose a pleading.
The general-conviction-sealing route stands in for three statutory subsections and may need the same split treatment Oregon needed. Flagged, not decided.
Whether the marijuana pardon route may be sold as record-clearing relief, given that its own controlling form says a pardon will not expunge the criminal history record.
Counsel review of every determination above.
remainingReview: Counsel review of the vehicle determinations and of the pardon-relief question. This record binds one official source to one route by verified bytes and maps the rest; it approves no output and opens no route.
